info.title: Sessionboard Public API
info.description: REST API for managing sessions, speakers, contacts, sponsors, exhibitors, and event data on the Sessionboard platform.

tags.name: Learning
tags.description:
Turn Media-section videos (webinars, recordings, uploads, clips) into a course: draft it from
videos, review and edit the draft, then publish it and assign it. Organization-level: paths
start at `/v1/organization/{orgId}/learning`, and the same operations are served under
`/v1/learning` with the organization taken from the token. Requires the preview scopes
`read:learning` / `write:learning`, which a token or OAuth client gets only when they are
named explicitly (not by default, and not listed in `scopes_supported`). The organization
must have Learning turned on, and the token's user needs the Lessons permissions.

tags.name: Learning workspace
tags.description: The self-serve Sessionboard Learning workspace: Home, courses, learners, putting a meeting on demand, credits and results, and publishing (which waits for a person's OK, `202 needs_approval`). Organization-level: paths start at `/v1/organization/{orgId}/learning/workspace`, and the same operations are served under `/v1/learning/workspace` with the organization taken from the token. Requires the preview scopes `read:learning` / `write:learning`, named explicitly. A key restricted to particular events cannot use it.

tags.name: Learning meetings
tags.description: Bring in a meeting from a registration platform (Cvent, Swoogo, Bizzabo and others) and turn its sessions into draft courses: the platforms and what each brings, the platform's events, the import and its progress. Nothing is written back to the platform, and nothing is published. Same scopes and paths as the Learning workspace (`…/learning/workspace/meetings`).

tags.name: Learning engagement
tags.description: Learners on the one engagement score: ranked learners, one learner across products, who to nudge, who is due for recertification, next courses for an event's people, the signal sources, and bringing Learning's records onto the score (`sync`, which sends nothing). Same scopes and paths as the Learning workspace (`…/learning/workspace/engagement`).

tags.name: Learning certifications
tags.description: The organization's certifications: what each requires and who holds it. Requires `read:learning`.

tags.name: Sites
tags.description: Build and edit a product's Site by API or chat: the Marketing event page, a Learning Site, an Awards Site. Every edit lands in the Site's draft; nothing goes live until you publish with the person's OK, and every publish is a version you can restore. Organization-level: paths start at `/v1/organization/{orgId}/sites`, and the same operations are served under `/v1/sites` with the organization taken from the token. Reads need `read:sites` or the Site's product scope (`read:marketing`, `read:learning`, `read:awards`); writes need the matching `write:` scope. The signed-in person's own access to the Site applies too.

get.description: Every certification in the organization (draft, published and retired), by name, with its required lessons and courses, how many lessons it takes and their total minutes, how many people hold it now, how many awards expire within 30 days, and how many people are assigned it and overdue. Reads only. The token's user needs the Lessons read permission. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/certifications`.

The Learning workspace home: who learns here (the setup answers and the door they imply, `companies` or `associations`), which sections lead, the counts behind the home tiles, what is ready for a person's review (course drafts, meeting courses still in draft, certifications about to lapse) and whether Learning is on for the organization (`module.on`). Counts are totals, never learner rows. Any member of the organization can read it, even before Learning is turned on. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace`.

Every course that is not archived (up to 200, most recently changed first) with where it came from (a meeting session, a synced catalog or written here), its credit by credit type, how many learners started it and how many completed it; plus up to 50 course drafts made from recordings (queued, generating, ready or failed) and the credit set on each. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/courses`.

get.summary: Get a course and its learners
get.description: One course as the course list shows it (source, credit, learners, completions) plus its number of steps that count, and up to 200 of the people taking it, most recent activity first, each with steps done, percent and whether they completed it. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/courses/{lessonId}`.

404.description: No such course in your organization (`Course could not be found`), or another organization.

get.description: Finds people in the organization by name or email, to open their learner view. Covers everyone in People, including someone who only claimed credit. Fewer than two characters returns no one; at most 20 matches, by last name. A teammate limited to some credits portfolios finds only those portfolios' people. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/learners`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a first name, last name or email. At least 2 characters to match anyone.

get.description: One learner: their courses with progress, certifications with status and expiry, assignments with due dates, sessions attended, and their credit by credit type with every claim and certificate, plus the paths of their transcript downloads. Read from the existing course progress, awards and credit records; nothing is copied. A teammate limited to some credits portfolios gets `404` for anyone outside them. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/learners/{personId}`.

404.description: No such person in your organization or portfolios (`Learner could not be found`), or another organization.

get.summary: List meetings that can go on demand
get.description: Up to 50 of the organization's events, newest first, that have recorded sessions, courses made from their sessions, or sessions brought in from a registration platform: what "put the meeting on demand" can start from. Each with its session count, sessions with recordings, and courses already published or in draft. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/on-demand`.

For each session of the event: its recording, faculty and missing faculty disclosures, credit by credit type, attendance count, the registration platform it came from, and whether it is a course yet (and whether that course still waits for a recording); plus totals for the event. Every value is read from the event's own records. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/on-demand/{eventId}`.

post.summary: Make draft courses from a meeting
post.description: Turns the event's sessions into draft courses, gathered into one course for the meeting ("<event> on demand"). Each course carries the session's recording, quiz, credit, faculty and disclosure decisions. By default only sessions with a recording are used; with `includeWithoutRecording`, sessions without one become drafts that wait for a recording. Up to 60 sessions per call: `remaining` says how many are left, so call again until it is `0`. Safe to repeat: a session that is already a course is never drafted twice, a waiting draft whose session now has a recording gets it (`attached`), and a draft nobody edited takes the session's new title and description (`refreshed`). With `dryRun` it only counts. Nothing is published and no one is notified; publishing is Publish a meeting on demand. Learners keep the credit they already claimed in the room. The token's user needs the Lessons create permission. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/on-demand/{eventId}`.

sessionIds.description: Only these sessions. Omit for every session of the event.

includeWithoutRecording.description: Also draft sessions with no recording yet, as courses waiting for one.

dryRun.description: Count what would be made; write nothing.

201.description: Drafted (or, with `dryRun`, counted). A dry run answers `LearningOnDemandDryRun`; otherwise `LearningOnDemandMakeResult`. When every session is already a course, `created` is `0` and `message` says so.

400.description: The body failed validation, `eventId` is not a whole number, or `No courses could be made from those sessions.`

post.summary: Publish a meeting on demand
post.description: Asks to publish the meeting's draft courses (all of them, or `lessonIds`). Publishing waits for a person: the call answers `202` with `status: needs_approval` and a link, and nothing is published until a person approves it in Sessionboard Learning; it then runs as them. When it runs, a course whose faculty has no disclosure on file, or that still waits for its recording, stays a draft and is listed as held with the reason. Do not call again while the request is pending. The token's user needs the Lessons update permission. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/on-demand/{eventId}/publish`.

lessonIds.description: Only these draft courses of the meeting. Omit for all of them.

prompt.description: What the person asked for, shown on the approval request.

post.summary: Publish a course
post.description: Asks to publish one course (draft to published), so the catalog and Learning Sites show it. Publishing waits for a person: the call answers `202` with `status: needs_approval` and a link, and nothing is published until a person approves it in Sessionboard Learning; it then runs as them. When it runs it is refused while any faculty member on the course has no disclosure on file, or when the course is archived. Do not call again for the same course while the request is pending. The token's user needs the Lessons update permission. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/courses/{lessonId}/publish`.

prompt.description: What the person asked for, shown on the approval request.

post.summary: Publish a reviewed course draft
post.description: Asks to publish a course drafted from a recording once a person has reviewed its suggested questions. Publishing waits for a person: the call answers `202` with `status: needs_approval` and a link, and nothing is published, assigned or announced until a person approves it in Sessionboard Learning; it then runs as them. When it runs, it is refused while any suggested question has not been accepted, edited or rejected by a person; rejected questions are taken out; the lessons, course and certification are published as in Publish and assign a course draft (with `assign` and `announce` as there); and the credit a person set on the draft goes on the course's last lesson. Reviewing the questions and setting credit are a person's and are not available through the API. The token's user needs the Lessons create and update permissions. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/drafts/{draftId}/publish`.

assign.description: Who must take it. Omit to publish without assigning.

allTeam.description: Everyone on the team, including people who join later.

allowPendingMedia.description: Publish even while clips are still being cut.

prompt.description: What the person asked for, shown on the approval request.

get.description: The Credits overview: whether credits are on for the workspace, the organization's credit types (the ones picked in setup first, marked `chosen`), credit issued by type, the 25 latest claims, events whose credit claiming is open, the credit goals per type and suggested goals (what a learner earned in the last 12 months, median and top quarter). Amounts are never added across credit types. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/credits`.

Results for the workspace: completions by month (last 6 months), credit claimed by credit type (last 12 months), up to 20 certifications with holders, expiring within 90 days and expired, the home counts, the door (companies read completions and certifications first, associations read credit first), and `claude_prompt`, a ready-made prompt with these numbers for building a dashboard in Claude. Nothing is sent anywhere. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/results`.

The organization's bank questions, newest first, 50 a page. A quiz page draws from the bank by tag with a `bank_draw` block (`{ tags, match, count, points? }`): publishing the course copies every matching live question into the quiz, and each attempt draws `count` of them per learner. `tags` narrows the list to questions that carry every tag (any of them with `match=any`), `q` to prompts that contain the text. Each item carries the question block (answers included), its type, the prompt as plain text, its tags and whether it is archived. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/question-bank`.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated tags, for example `pharmacology,module-2`.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: `all` (default): questions with every tag. `any`: questions with at least one.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text the prompt contains.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: `true` lists archived questions instead of live ones.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many questions to skip, for the next page.

get.description: The tags in use on live bank questions, with how many questions carry each, most used first (up to 200). Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/question-bank/tags`.

post.summary: Add, edit, archive or restore a bank question
post.description: `create` adds a question (`question`, a question block with its answers, and up to 10 `tags`). `update` changes a question's block, its tags or both (`itemId`). `archive` takes a question out of future draws and `restore` puts it back. A quiz that already drew a question keeps its copy until its course is published again. The token's user needs the Lessons update permission. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/question-bank/manage`.

itemId.description: The bank question. Required for every action except `create`.

question.description: A question block (the same shape a quiz page uses), answers included.

get.summary: List registration platforms a meeting can come from
get.description: Every registration platform a meeting can be brought in from, whether it is connected, and what comes across from each: sessions, speakers (on the sessions they present, or as contacts only), recordings (never sent with sessions; added after) and attendance (session check-ins, when the connection's sign-in can read them), with the one-line summary to show a person. Worked out from each connector and the live connection, not promised by hand. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/meetings/sources`.

The connected platform's events, newest first, each with the Sessionboard event it was already brought into (`imported_event_id`), so importing it again updates that event instead of making a second one. When the platform is not connected, `connected` is `false` and `events` is empty. Reads the platform; writes nothing. The token's user needs permission to view integrations. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/meetings/sources/{appId}/events`.

post.summary: Bring in a meeting from a registration platform
post.description: Makes the platform's event a Sessionboard event and queues the import of its sessions, speakers (on the sessions they present, where the platform reads that), tracks and session check-ins. Nothing is written to the platform, nothing is published and no one is notified. Safe to repeat: an event brought in before is updated (new sessions added, changed ones updated unless someone edited them in Sessionboard), never duplicated. With `dryRun` it reads the platform's event and says what would happen (`status: preview`), writing nothing. The import runs in the background: poll Get an imported meeting with `jobId` until `import.state` is `done`, then make courses from it. Always answers `202`; `status` says what happened: `queued`, `preview`, `not_connected` (with `connect_url`, where a person connects the platform), `needs_remote_event`, `not_available` or `managed_on_platform`. The token's user needs the Lessons create permission and permission to view integrations. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/meetings/import`.

remoteEventId.description: The platform's event id, from List a registration platform's events.

dryRun.description: Say what would happen; write nothing.

400.description: The body failed validation, or the connection has no event with that id (`There is no <platform> event with id <id> on this connection.`).

post.summary: Bring in a meeting and draft courses, step by step
post.description: "Import last year's meeting and make courses" in three steps. `preview` (the default) writes nothing: with no `appId` it lists the platforms and what each brings; with an `appId`, that platform's events and `suggested` (the latest one that already happened); with a `remoteEventId`, what the import would do. `import` brings the event in, as Bring in a meeting (needs `appId` and `remoteEventId`; answers `job_id` and `event`). `draft` makes draft courses from every session of the imported event (needs `eventId`; pass `jobId` to get `status: still_importing` while the import runs), the ones without a recording waiting for one. Nothing is published and no one is notified: publishing is Publish a meeting on demand, which a person approves. Credit is never set here. The token's user needs the Lessons create permission and permission to view integrations. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/meetings/import-for-learning`.

eventId.description: The Sessionboard event the import made (`draft` step).

jobId.description: The import job (`draft` step waits for it).

200.description: The step's answer: `step` plus, for `preview`, the platforms (as List registration platforms), one platform's events (as List a registration platform's events, with `suggested` and `message`) or an import preview (as Bring in a meeting with `status: preview`); for `import`, the import (as Bring in a meeting); for `draft`, `status: still_importing` or `status: drafted` with the result of Make draft courses from a meeting and `next`.

400.description: The body failed validation; `Importing needs appId and remoteEventId.`; `Drafting needs the eventId the import returned.`; the connection has no event with that id; or `No courses could be made from those sessions.`

404.description: Another organization, or (`draft` step) the event is not in your organization (`Event could not be found`).

get.description: A meeting brought in from a registration platform: with `jobId`, the import's progress (`running`, `done` or `failed`) and up to 12 notes on what did not come across; and the meeting as Preview a meeting on demand sees it (sessions, recordings, faculty, attendance, courses and the ones waiting for a recording). Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/meetings/{eventId}`.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The `job_id` the import answered. Omit and `import` is `null`.

get.description: Everyone learning (a course, quiz, credit claim or certification, or a session or event attended), ranked by Learning's view of the one engagement score, where learning counts more and events and campaigns still count. Each with the score, its band, why (for example "72 = 3 courses · 4.5 credits · certified · 2 webinars"), the overall score and what they did. `counts` gives the number in each band before `band` filters. A teammate limited to some credits portfolios ranks only those portfolios' people. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/learners`.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Only people tied to this event.

total.description: Learners in the list after `band`, before paging.

get.description: One person across every product: the score (Learning's view and overall) with its parts and why, a timeline across meetings, campaigns and courses, credit owed this cycle against the credit goal, certifications coming up for renewal, the next three courses with the reason for each, and their events and Marketing activity. A teammate limited to some credits portfolios gets `404` for anyone outside them. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/learners/{personId}`.

404.description: No such person in your organization or portfolios, or they have no email (`Learner could not be found`), or another organization.

get.description: Learning's view of the engagement score, with its why, for up to 200 people by People id: the score chips for a page of learners. Ids that are not well-formed, have no email, or are outside the caller's credits portfolios are left out. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/scores`.

parameters.name: personIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated People ids (UUIDs). The first 200 are read.

get.description: People worth a nudge, most urgent first, each with the reason, a sentence of detail and the next course that answers it: a certification up for renewal (`renewal`), a course stalled for two weeks (`stalled`), credit owed late in the credit cycle (`credit_owed`), or a session attended whose course they have not taken (`earn_credit`). Reads only; nothing is sent. A nudge goes out through a Keep learning campaign, on a person's OK. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/nudge`.

counts.description: People per reason. Absent when there is no one to nudge.

get.description: Learning engagement over time: how many learners are in each band now and 30 days ago, how many moved up a band and which learning activities moved them (points added), and 30-day outcomes (courses completed, people certified, people who claimed credit and credit claimed). Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/results`.

People whose certification expires within `withinDays`, or lapsed in the last 90 days and has not been renewed, soonest first (up to 500), each with the next course that counts toward renewal. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/recertification`.

The next courses for an event's people (`eventId`) or for named people (`emails`): up to two per person with the reason for each, and the courses most of them would take. Reads only; nothing is sent. Sending recommendations is a Keep learning campaign. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/recommend`.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event whose people to recommend for. Takes precedence over `emails`.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: Comma-separated emails. The first 200 are read.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: People returned.

404.description: The event is not in your organization (`Event could not be found`), or another organization.

get.description: How connected the Learning workspace is: every source that feeds learner engagement (courses, certifications, credits, your meetings, Marketing campaigns, registration and webinar platforms, files), whether each is connected, what each brought in over the last 30 days, an estimate of what an unconnected one would add (only from this organization's own history, else none), the capabilities connected sources turn on, the next best connection, and recent signals. Reads only. Requires `read:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/sources`.

post.summary: Bring Learning activity into engagement now
post.description: Records Learning activity as engagement signals now instead of waiting for the next scheduled run: course progress, quizzes, credit claims, certifications and session attendance from the last `days` days. Safe to repeat: a re-run writes nothing new. Sends nothing. The token's user needs the Lessons update permission. Requires `write:learning`; refused for a key restricted to particular events. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/engagement/sync`.

post.summary: Import questions from GIFT, Aiken or CSV
post.description: Reads a GIFT, Aiken or CSV file (sent as `text`) and lists every question found as a row, ready or with its problems. Without `commit` nothing is written. With `commit: true` the ready rows are added to the bank; rows with problems are only left out when `skipInvalid` is `true`, and the answer lists every row not imported with its reason. Up to 1 MB and 500 questions. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/question-bank/import`.

skipInvalid.description: Import the ready rows when other rows have problems.

200.description: The preview, or what was imported.

fatal.description: Why nothing could be read (an empty file

post.summary: Get an upload URL for a course package
post.description: A 15-minute upload URL for a SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004, xAPI or cmi5 zip (up to 500 MB). `PUT` the bytes to `url` with exactly the returned `headers`, then call Add a course package with `key`. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/packages/presign`.

get.description: The organization's SCORM, xAPI and cmi5 packages, newest first. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/packages`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words in the title.

post.summary: Add a course package
post.description: Registers an uploaded zip. It is unpacked and every file checked in the background (no paths outside the package, no links, no programs), and the answer is `202` with `status: processing`. Poll Get a course package until `status` is `ready` (or `failed`, with `error`). A lesson plays it with a `package` block. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/packages`.

key.description: The `key` from Get an upload URL for a course package.

title.description: Leave out to use the course's own title.

get.description: One package, while it unpacks and after. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/packages/{packageId}`.

post.summary: Rename, archive, restore or retry a course package
post.description: `rename` with `title`; `archive` (lessons already playing it keep playing it) and `restore`; `retry` unpacks a failed package again. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/packages/{packageId}/manage`.

put.summary: Set a course's price and member price
put.description: What learners pay for a course, in cents. `amountCents: 0` makes it free again; `memberAmountCents` is what members pay (0 = free for members, `null` removes the member price). A member is a learner marked Member, or anyone the organization's AMS reports as a current member. Waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Requires `write:learning`. Also at `PUT /v1/learning/workspace/courses/{lessonId}/price`.

amountCents.description: The price in cents. 0 = free; a paid course costs at least 50.

memberAmountCents.description: What members pay, in cents. null removes it.

get.description: Every coupon with its code, discount, the courses it works on (empty = every course), dates, use limit, how many times it was used and its state (`live`, `scheduled`, `expired`, `used_up`, `archived`). Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/coupons`.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: `true` for stopped coupons instead of live ones.

amount.description: Percent off, or cents off for kind amount.

post.summary: Create, change, stop or restore a coupon
post.description: A coupon is a code and a discount (`kind` percent or amount). It works on every course unless `lessonIds` names some; dates and a use limit are optional. Coupons come off after the member price. `archive` stops a coupon and `restore` brings it back. Waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/coupons/manage`.

code.description: Letters and numbers; one is made up when left out on create.

amount.description: Percent off (1–100), or cents off for kind amount.

lessonIds.description: Only these courses. Empty = every course.

get.description: Course orders, newest first: the learner, the course, when, what they paid, the list price, member price or coupon applied, and whether they still have access (`active`, or `removed`). Totals per currency count paid orders. `selling.payments.ready` says whether card payments are on. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/sales`.

post.summary: Remove a buyer's access
post.description: Ends the learner's access to the order's course. The sale stays on record. A refund in the payment gateway keeps access until this is called. Waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Needs the permission that manages plan and billing, or an organization admin (`403` otherwise). Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/sales/{orderId}/remove-access`.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order id (from List course sales).

post.summary: Refund a course order
post.description: Refunds a paid order in full through the payment gateway that took it (Spreedly credits the original charge). The order becomes `refunded` and the learner gets a refund email. The learner keeps the course unless `removeAccess` is `true`. Refused (400) for an order that charged nothing (use Remove a buyer's access) or is already refunded, and when the gateway does not accept the refund (its reason is in `message`; nothing was refunded). Waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Needs the permission that manages plan and billing, or an organization admin (`403` otherwise). Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/sales/{orderId}/refund`.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The paid order (from List course sales).

removeAccess.description: true = also end the learner's access. Default false: refunds keep access.

get.summary: Read whether card payments are on
get.description: Whether the organization's payment gateway is connected (`ready`), which one, whether it is in test mode, and the gateways it can connect (100+ are supported). Connecting a gateway takes the organization's payment keys, and turning card payments off decides where money goes, so a person does both in Sessionboard (Site › Selling); there is no API for them. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/payments`.

gateway.description: The connected gateway: name, test mode.

gateways.description: The gateways the Get paid step offers.

put.summary: Set a learner's member status and license
put.description: `member` decides whether the learner gets member prices. The license (number, two-letter state, profession) is what CE Broker matches credit to. Empty strings clear a value. Waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Requires `write:learning`. Also at `PUT /v1/learning/workspace/learners/{personId}/profile`.

get.description: Setup (provider number, default profession, course numbers, `mode` mock or live, whether it needs a real CE Broker account), the credited courses, a summary (ready, missing, reported, failed) and every earned credit on a numbered course with the learner's license and status. `direct_submit` says whether sending is on the plan (Sessionboard Enterprise). Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/reporting/ce-broker`.

rows.description: One per earned credit; `status` ready, missing, reported or failed, with what is missing.

put.description: The provider number, a default profession for learners who have not given theirs, and a CE Broker course number per credited course (`null` removes one). Waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`). Requires `write:learning`. Also at `PUT /v1/learning/workspace/reporting/ce-broker`.

courseNumbers.description: Course id → CE Broker course number (20-123456).

uploadKey.description: The CE Broker upload key, for a live account. Write-only; never returned.

get.description: The roster as text with its filename, on every plan. `format=xml` (default) is CE Broker's upload format with the ready rows; `format=csv` lists every row with its status. The person uploads the XML in CE Broker's provider portal. 400 when nothing is ready or the provider number is missing. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/workspace/reporting/ce-broker/export`.

where.description: Where a person downloads the same file in Sessionboard.

post.summary: Send ready credit to CE Broker
post.description: `dryRun: true` counts what would be sent, on every plan. Sending is Sessionboard Enterprise (`403 enterprise_only` otherwise: export the roster instead) and waits for a person's OK (`202 needs_approval`), because it sends learners' names and license numbers to a state-board system. Until a live CE Broker account is connected it runs in practice mode: nothing leaves Sessionboard and nothing is recorded. A row is never sent twice. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/workspace/reporting/ce-broker/submit`.

get.summary: List videos a course can be made from
get.description: Media-section recordings, uploads and clips, newest first. A course is written from what is said, so only items with `has_transcript: true` can be used (a clip uses its recording's transcript). Requires `read:learning`. Also served at `GET /v1/learning/media` with the organization taken from the token.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `video` for recordings and uploads, `clip` for clips cut from them. Omit for both.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Words from the title.

get.description: The organization's lessons and courses (series), with ids and external keys — what an assignment can target. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/library`.
Course drafts made from videos, newest first. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/drafts`.

post.summary: Draft a course from videos
post.description: Starts making a course from 1–10 videos or clips. The videos are checked now (same organization, a transcript, no cuts); then the course is generated in the background: lesson-sized segments, a clip cut for each, and per lesson a short reading, in-video questions and a quiz, every question grounded in that clip's transcript. Answers `202` with the draft (`status: queued`); poll `GET /v1/organization/{orgId}/learning/drafts/{draftId}` until `status` is `ready` or `failed` (usually a minute or two per video). Nothing is published and no one is notified. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/drafts/create`.

mediaItemIds.description: Videos / clips from List videos, in course order.

title.description: Course title. Defaults to the video's title when there is one video.

audience.description: Who the course is for. Shapes the writing; it does not decide who is assigned.

certification.description: Add a certification earned by completing every lesson.

validityMonths.description: How long the certification lasts. Omit for never expires.

checkpointsPerLesson.description: Questions that pause the video, per lesson. Default 2.

quizQuestions.description: Final quiz questions per lesson. Default 4.

maxLessonsPerVideo.description: Upper bound on lessons from one long video, default 8. Exceeded only when fewer lessons would each run past 10 minutes.

poll.description: Internal path of the draft; poll the Get a course draft operation.

400.description: A video is not in this organization, has no transcript, or has cuts.

get.description: While generating: `status` and `progress`. When `ready`: the `bundle` (lessons, the course, the certification), the `diff` publishing would make, `warnings` (questions left out because the clip doesn't answer them) and `media` — per clip, its `status` and a short-lived playable `url`. Requires `read:learning`. Also at `GET /v1/learning/drafts/{draftId}`.

404.description: Not found — also returned for another organization's draft.

put.summary: Save edits to a course draft
put.description: Replaces the draft's bundle with your edited copy (send the whole bundle — anything left out is dropped) and returns the draft with a fresh `diff`. Pass the draft's `updated_at` from the read you edited as `baseUpdatedAt`: if the draft changed since, the save answers `409` with `code: COURSE_DRAFT_STALE` and writes nothing. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `PUT /v1/learning/drafts/{draftId}`.

200.description: Saved; the draft as in Get a course draft.

400.description: The bundle failed validation (the message names the lesson and question).

409.description: The draft changed since `baseUpdatedAt` (`code: COURSE_DRAFT_STALE`, with the current `updated_at`).

post.summary: Publish and assign a course draft
post.description: Publishes the draft's lessons, course and certification to every learner in the organization. Lessons upsert by key, so publishing an edited draft again updates the same lessons and keeps learners' progress. With `assign`, assigns the certification (or the course when there is none) and messages each assignee (Slack DM, or email when Slack can't reach them); repeating the same `assign` does not assign or message again. With `announce.slackChannelId`, posts the announcement in that channel. Refused while clips are still being cut unless `allowPendingMedia`. The token's user needs the Lessons create and update permissions. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/drafts/{draftId}/apply`.

allTeam.description: Everyone on the team, including people who join later.

200.description: Published; the draft with `apply_result` (`diff`, the assignment and its delivery report).

400.description: A clip could not be cut, or there is nothing to assign.

403.description: Token lacks `write:learning`, the user lacks the Lessons permissions, clips are still being cut, or the draft changed or is being published (reload it).

post.summary: Assign a certification, course or lesson
post.description: Assigns already-published training to the whole team or named teammates and messages each of them. Requires `write:learning`. Also at `POST /v1/learning/assignments/create`.

201.description: Assigned; `payload.assignment` and `payload.delivery` (who was messaged, and how).

get.description: The organization's Sites in Marketing, Learning and Awards, most recently changed first (up to 200). Each carries its `revision` (send it back on your next write) and whether it has unpublished changes. Also at `GET /v1/sites`.

parameters.name: product
parameters.description: Only this product's Sites.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Only this event's Sites (Marketing event pages).

post.summary: Make a Site
post.description: Makes a product's first Site with no setup, from the organization's own data and Brand Kit: a Learning Site from its courses, an Awards Site with its home in the draft, or a Marketing page for an event (`eventId`). Pass `url` to rebuild an existing page: its text, menu and images come back as `source_page` for you to turn into edits. Nothing is published. Also at `POST /v1/sites/make`.

brief.description: What the Site is for, in the person's words.

eventId.description: Marketing only; the event the page is for.

200.description: The new Site, read as in Get a Site, plus `source_page` when you sent `url`.

source_page.description: The page at `url`, read for you to rebuild (title, headings, text, links, images).

400.description: A missing `eventId` for Marketing, or a `url` that could not be read.

get.description: The Site as its draft stands: its pages with their blocks, the menu, the theme, the roles you can preview as, the block catalog (every block kind this Site takes, with its JSON Schema), what Publish would change, and the rules for editing. Also at `GET /v1/sites/{siteId}`.

404.description: Not found — also returned for another organization's Site.

put.description: Applies up to 60 edits, in order, to the draft. Visitors see nothing until you publish. Send the `revision` you last read as `baseRevision`: if the Site changed since, the call answers `409` with `code: SITE_DRAFT_STALE` and writes nothing; read it again and retry. All edits apply or none do; a block that fails its schema answers `400` naming the block. Also at `PUT /v1/sites/{siteId}/draft`.

baseRevision.description: The `revision` from your last read (three timestamps joined by dots; send it back as is).

brandKitId.description: The Brand Kit the Site follows, applied when it is published.

200.description: Saved. The new `revision`, what changed, and the Site's pages and diff.

400.description: An edit could not apply (the message names it), or a block failed its schema (`details` per block).

post.summary: Discard a Site's draft
post.description: Throws away every unpublished change; the draft goes back to what is live. Confirm with the person first. Also at `POST /v1/sites/{siteId}/draft/discard`.

get.description: The draft against what is live, in pages, blocks and settings, with one plain sentence per change in `summary` — show it to the person before they approve a publish. Also at `GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/diff`.

get.summary: Preview a Site as a role on a device
get.description: A short-lived link to the draft as one role sees it on one device, plus a structured description of what that role sees (pages and blocks), for clients that cannot open the link. Roles depend on the product: `visitor` and `invited` (Marketing), `visitor` and `learner` (Learning), `visitor`, `submitter`, `evaluator` and, on event portals, `speaker` (Awards). Also at `GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/preview`.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description: One of the Site's `roles` (default `visitor`).

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: `home`, a page id, slug or exact title (default `home`).

400.description: A role this Site does not have.

post.summary: Publish a Site
post.description: The draft goes live. Only after the person has seen the diff (and a preview) and said OK: send `confirmed: true` and the `revision` of the diff they approved; an edit made after their OK answers `409`. Called by an AI assistant, it answers `202` with `status: needs_approval` and a link: a person approves it in Sessionboard, and it runs as them. Every publish is a version you can restore. Also at `POST /v1/sites/{siteId}/publish`.

revision.description: The `revision` of the diff the person approved.

confirmed.description: `true` only after the person said OK.

202.description: Waiting for a person: `status: needs_approval`, `approval_id` and `url` to approve it in Sessionboard.

409.description: The draft changed after the approved `revision` (`code: SITE_DRAFT_STALE`).

get.description: Every publish, newest first, with a plain-language summary of what it changed. A Site's first publish also keeps the Site as it was before (`source: baseline`). Also at `GET /v1/sites/{siteId}/versions`.

post.summary: Restore a version into the draft
post.description: Copies a version into the draft so the person can look it over; nothing goes live until it is published. Also at `POST /v1/sites/{siteId}/versions/{versionId}/restore`.

200.description: Restored into the draft; the new `revision`, the version number and the diff against live.

404.description: No such version on this Site.

ApiKey.name: x-access-token
ApiKey.description: Organization API token. Generate from Organization Settings → API Tokens.

BearerToken.description: OAuth 2.1 access token. Obtained via the OAuth PKCE flow at `/oauth/token`.

LearningOrgId.name: orgId
LearningOrgId.description: Your organization ID. Any other organization returns `404`.

LearningLessonId.name: lessonId
LearningLessonId.description: The course id (from List courses and course drafts).

LearningPersonId.name: personId
LearningPersonId.description: The People id (from Find a learner or Rank learners by engagement).

LearningEventId.name: eventId
LearningEventId.description: The Sessionboard event. Another organization's event answers `401`.

SitesOrgId.name: orgId
SitesOrgId.description: Your organization ID. Any other organization returns `404`.

SiteVersionId.name: versionId
SiteVersionId.description: The version's `id` from List a Site's versions.

updated_at.description: Send back as `baseUpdatedAt` when you save.

diff.description: What publishing would do — `created` / `updated` / `unchanged` for lessons, courses and certifications.

media.description: Per clip id — `status` (ready, processing, failed, missing), a short-lived `url`, `duration_s`, `poster_url`.

CourseBundle.description: Lessons, the course and the certification. A lesson's watch step plays a clip (`mediaItemId`) and may carry `checkpoints` — questions with `atSeconds`, seconds into the clip. A question has `prompt`, `type`, `options`, `answer` (multi-select, ordering and matching answers are JSON strings), optional `config` and `feedback` (`correct`, `incorrect`, `hint`). Keys are permanent: publishing upserts by key.

LearningCoursePackage.description: A SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004, xAPI or cmi5 course package.

mastery_score.description: The pass mark the package sets

skipped.description: Files in the zip that aren't served, and why.

LearningError.description: Gateway errors carry `error` (a code) and `message`. Errors from Learning itself carry `status`, `success: false`, `message`, `name`, and sometimes `code` (and `feature` or `paused_at`).

url.description: Where a person approves or declines it, in Sessionboard Learning.

note.description: Says nothing was sent or published and not to call again.

title.description: The approval card's headline, e.g. `Publish the course “Intro to Safety”`.

summary.description: What the person asked the assistant, when given (`From “…”`), else empty.

remedy.description: Set only when a run failed for a reason a person can fix in one step.

requirements.description: Lessons and courses (series) that must be completed.

validity_months.description: How long an award lasts. `null` never expires.

holders.description: People holding it now (active, not expired).

overdue.description: Assigned people past their due date.

lead.description: The section that leads (associations lead with credits, companies with certifications).

review.description: What is waiting on a person, up to 5 drafts, 3 meetings and 3 certifications.

on.description: Whether Learning is on for the organization.

LearningWorkspaceProfile.description: The setup answers, with the defaults they imply.

assistant.description: The assistant jobs switched on. All are on until asked.

asked.description: Which setup questions have been answered.

overdue.description: Assignments past due and not completed.

credit_30d.description: Credit claimed in the last 30 days

transcripts.description: People with at least one credit claim.

id.description: The draft id, the event id (as text) or the certification id.

LearningCourseCredit.description: The course's credit by credit type. Types are never added together: `amount` and `type` are set only when there is one type; `label` lists each (e.g. `1.00 AMA PRA Category 1 Credit · 1.00 ANCC Contact Hours`).

completed.description: People who finished every step that counts.

steps.description: Steps that count toward completion (claim and survey steps do not).

credit.description: The credit a person set on the draft, applied on publish.

percent.description: `null` when the course has no steps that count.

courses.description: Up to 200 courses they touched, most recent activity first.

days_left.description: `null` once expired or when it never expires.

types.description: Credit by credit type, largest total first.

attended.description: Up to 200 sessions attended, newest first.

imported.description: Brought in from a registration platform.

disclosures_missing.description: Faculty with no disclosure on file.

credit.description: The session's credit, or the credit set on the course made from it (the course's wins per type). Types are never added together.

source.description: The registration platform it came from.

recording_ready.description: Waiting, and the session now has a recording; make courses again to add it.

disclosures_missing.description: Sessions with a faculty disclosure missing.

imported.description: Sessions brought in from a registration platform.

waiting_for_recording.description: Of the courses made, how many wait for a recording. Absent when `created` is `0`.

attached.description: Waiting drafts that got their recording.

refreshed.description: Untouched drafts that took the session's new title and description.

series_id.description: The meeting's course ("<event> on demand"). `null` when nothing was made.

courses.description: The draft courses made. Absent when `created` is `0`.

LearningQuestionBankItem.description: A question in the organization's question bank.

question.description: The question block, answers included; its `id` is the bank question's id.

enabled.description: Whether credits are on for the workspace.

types.description: Up to 100 credit types, those picked in setup first.

increment.description: Smallest step credit is rounded down to

totals.description: Live credit claimed by credit type, largest first.

claim_sites.description: Up to 20 events whose credit claiming is open.

goals.description: Credit goals, one per credit type.

goal_suggestions.description: What a learner earned of each type in the last 12 months, rounded up to a quarter.

monthly.description: Course completions by month, last 6 months.

credit_by_type.description: Live credit claimed by credit type, last 12 months.

certifications.description: Up to 20 certifications that are not retired, most holders first.

claude_prompt.description: A prompt with these numbers for building a dashboard in Claude. Nothing is sent.

LearningRegistrationAppIdValue.description: A registration platform. Today sessions can be brought in from `cvent`, `swoogo` and `bizzabo`; the others answer `not_available` (List registration platforms says why).

importable.description: Sessions can be brought in from it.

on_sessions.description: Speakers arrive on the sessions they present, so faculty carry over.

needs_new_sign_in.description: The connection's sign-in cannot read attendees or check-ins.

line.description: One line to show a person.

imported_event_id.description: The Sessionboard event it was brought into before.

supported.description: Whether the platform can list events. Absent when not connected.

connect_url.description: `not_connected` only: where a person connects the platform in Sessionboard Learning.

event.description: The Sessionboard event. On `preview`: `id` (`null` when one will be made), `name`, `will_create`. After an import: `id`, `name`, `created`; `null` when nothing was queued and no event was made.

reasons.description: Per kind that is not brought in, why.

job_id.description: The import job; pass it as `jobId` to Get an imported meeting.

LearningMeetingForLearningStep.description: `step` plus the fields of the answer it wraps (List registration platforms, List a registration platform's events, Bring in a meeting, or Make draft courses from a meeting).

status.description: `still_importing` or `drafted` on the `draft` step; on `import` and an import preview, as in Bring in a meeting.

suggested.description: `preview` with an `appId`: the latest of its events that already happened.

notes.description: What did not come across, in the import's words.

import.description: `null` without `jobId`, or when the job is not this organization's.

LearningEngagementLines.description: The scores where the bands start (default 50 and 80).

LearningEngagementChip.description: Learning's view of the one engagement score (learning counts more), with the overall score beside it.

why.description: The score as a sentence, e.g. `72 = 3 courses · 4.5 credits · certified · 2 webinars`.

LearningNextLesson.description: A course worth taking next, with the reason in words a learner can read.

credit_owed.description: Credit owed this cycle against the credit goal. `null` without a goal.

people.description: People with at least one course to take next.

courses.description: Courses picked, by how many people they suit.

moved_up.description: People who moved up a band in 30 days.

start.description: Where to start a built-in source that has nothing yet.

estimate.description: What an unconnected source would add. `per_month` is `null` when there is nothing to go on.

next_best.description: The connection that would add the most.

revision.description: Send back as `baseRevision` on your next write.

config.description: The block's settings, as its schema in `block_catalog` describes.

ref.description: `home`, or how to refer to the page in an edit.

id.description: `null` for a page that is new in the draft.

last_write.description: Who wrote the draft last (a person, Ask, or an MCP client) and when.

roles.description: Who you can preview the Site as.

has_pages.description: `false` for a one-page Site (the Marketing event page): use page `home`.

block_catalog.description: Every block kind this Site takes, with a label, a JSON Schema for `config` and an example.

rules.description: How to edit this Site, in plain sentences.

SiteOp.description: One edit. Pages are named by `home`, a page id, a slug or the exact title. `page.add` takes `page` (`title`, optional `slug`, `blocks`, `hidden`, `visibility`) and `before`; `page.update` takes `page` and any of `title`, `slug`, `hidden`, `visibility`; `page.move` takes `page` and `before`; `page.remove` takes `page`. `block.add` takes `page`, `block` (`kind`, `config`, optional `id`, `hidden`) and `before`; `block.update` takes `page` and `block` (`id`, `config` merged into the block unless `replace: true`, `hidden`); `block.move` takes `page`, `block.id`, optional `to_page` and `before`; `block.remove` takes `page` and `block.id`. `nav.set` takes `items` (each `kind` `page`, `url` or `form`, with `label`); `nav.reset` goes back to the pages. `theme.set` takes `theme` (`primary`, `accent`, `text` as hex, `gradient` [two hex], `font`, `logoUrl`, `mode` `light` / `dark` / `auto`, `followBrandKit`). `site.update` takes `name`.

summary.description: One plain sentence per change, for the person to read.

preview_url.description: Opens the draft as this role; expires at `expires_at`.

sees.description: What this role sees, for clients that cannot open the link.

version.description: `0` is the Site before its first versioned publish.

LearningForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:learning` (reads) or `write:learning` (writes). Legacy tokens with no scopes cannot write.
- `FORBIDDEN` — Learning is not on for the organization, or the token's user lacks the Lessons permission.

LearningEventUnauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired token, or the event does not belong to your organization (`Event does not belong to your organization`).

LearningOrgNotFound.description: `orgId` is not your organization (`error: NOT_FOUND`, `message: Organization not found`).

LearningBadRequest.description: A path, query or body value failed validation, or an unknown body property was sent. `message` names the field. (A `source` object naming the assistant, with the person's `prompt`, is accepted on every write and removed before validation.) For an `{eventId}` path that is not a whole number: `error: VALIDATION_ERROR`, `eventId must be a valid integer`.

LearningWorkspaceForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:learning` (reads) or `write:learning` (writes). Legacy tokens with no scopes cannot write.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED` — the token is restricted to particular events: "The Learning workspace covers every event and learner in the organization, so this API key (restricted to particular events) cannot use it. Use a key without an event restriction."
- `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` (`feature: lessons_credits`) — Learning is not on for the organization.
- `FORBIDDEN` — the token's user is not an active member of the organization, or lacks the Lessons permission the operation needs.

value.message: The Learning workspace covers every event and learner in the organization, so this API key (restricted to particular events) cannot use it. Use a key without an event restriction.
Feature 'lessons_credits' is not enabled for this organization
value.name: FeatureNotEnabledError

LearningWorkspaceEventForbidden.description:
As for every Learning workspace operation:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:learning` (reads) or `write:learning` (writes). Legacy tokens with no scopes cannot write.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED` — the token is restricted to particular events: "The Learning workspace covers every event and learner in the organization, so this API key (restricted to particular events) cannot use it. Use a key without an event restriction."
- `EVENT_ARCHIVED` — the event is archived.
- `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` (`feature: lessons_credits`) — Learning is not on for the organization.
- `FORBIDDEN` — the token's user is not an active member of the organization, or lacks the Lessons permission the operation needs.

LearningMeetingsForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:learning` (reads) or `write:learning` (writes). Legacy tokens with no scopes cannot write.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED` — the token is restricted to particular events: "Bringing in a meeting reaches the organization's registration platforms and every event, so this API key (restricted to particular events) cannot use it. Use a key without an event restriction."
- `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` (`feature: lessons_credits`) — Learning is not on for the organization.
- `FORBIDDEN` — the token's user is not an active member of the organization, lacks the Lessons permission, or (listing a platform's events, importing) lacks permission to view integrations (`You need permission to view integrations to use Apps`).

example.message: Bringing in a meeting reaches the organization's registration platforms and every event, so this API key (restricted to particular events) cannot use it. Use a key without an event restriction.

LearningMeetingsEventForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:learning`.
- `ORG_WIDE_TOKEN_REQUIRED` — the token is restricted to particular events: "Bringing in a meeting reaches the organization's registration platforms and every event, so this API key (restricted to particular events) cannot use it. Use a key without an event restriction."
- `EVENT_ARCHIVED` — the event is archived.
- `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` (`feature: lessons_credits`) — Learning is not on for the organization.
- `FORBIDDEN` — the token's user is not an active member of the organization, or lacks the Lessons read permission.

LearningNeedsApproval.description: Waiting for a person. Nothing was published or sent: a person approves or declines the request in Sessionboard Learning (`payload.url`), and it then runs as them. Do not call again.

LearningAssistantsPaused.description: A person has paused connected assistants for the organization or the event (`code: AGENT_WRITES_PAUSED`). Ask them to resume it in Sessionboard before trying again.

example.message: A person has paused connected assistants in Sessionboard. Ask them to resume it from their workspace before trying again.
example.name: AgentWritesPausedError

LearningTooManyRequests.description:
- The token's request limit (100 requests per 15 minutes per bucket by default — see [Rate Limiting](/rate-limiting)). Wait `Retry-After` seconds.
- `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (writes) — the token's daily write quota (10,000 a day). Resets at midnight UTC.

SitesForbidden.description:
- `SCOPE_REQUIRED` — the token lacks `read:sites` (or `read:marketing`, `read:learning`, `read:awards`) for reads, or the matching `write:` scope for writes.
- `FORBIDDEN` — the token's user cannot edit this Site.
